eventMetadata.context_description: **Current observational data and forecast consensus from meteorological sources drive the near-certain market-implied odds for a 28°C high in Paris on September 6.** Official guidance, including Météo-France-aligned reports, describes a very cloudy day with temperatures rising from morning lows near 17°C to an afternoon peak of 28–30°C under moderate southeast winds of 10–25 km/h, before easing slightly in the evening. Numerical models such as GFS align on this range, supported by surface observations showing readings around 28–29°C midday. Historical September 6 averages near 23°C and the absence of strong high-pressure ridging or clear skies that could push extremes higher reinforce the tight clustering. Only unexpected late-day warming or station-specific microclimate effects could realistically shift the recorded maximum away from 28°C.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by the Hong Kong Observatory in degrees Celsius on 6 Sep '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from the Hong Kong Observatory, specifically the "Absolute Daily Max (deg. C)" the specified date once information is finalized in the relevant "Daily Extract", available here: https://www.weather.gov.hk/en/cis/climat.htm

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the seventh day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

This market will resolve once data for this date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the seventh day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures in Celsius to one decimal place (eg, 9.1°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Any revisions to temperatures recorded after data is initially published for this market's timeframe will not be considered for this market's resolution.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Trader consensus has converged on 30°C as the official daily maximum at the Hong Kong Observatory because real-time observations and HKO data show the temperature peaking at or very near that threshold amid partly cloudy skies, scattered showers, and light winds.** 

Daytime readings reached approximately 30–31°C across urban stations before stabilizing, consistent with seasonal norms for early September when typical highs hover around 30–31°C under similar atmospheric conditions. With the observation window closing and no late-day intensification evident in official monitoring, alternative outcomes carry negligible implied probability. A realistic challenge would require an unforecasted late surge above 30°C or a post hoc data revision from the HKO, both improbable given converging station reports and model guidance.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=opkc

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: **Current forecasts from the National Weather Service and private models show a sunny September 6 with northeast flow moderating temperatures, producing a high in the upper 70s across the Chicago area.** Lake Michigan’s influence keeps readings cooler near the shoreline while inland spots reach the mid-to-upper 70s under clear skies and light winds around 10 mph. No significant warm-air advection or model disagreement has emerged to shift the outlook, leaving the market-implied odds tightly aligned with official guidance and real-time observations.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=kmia

This market will resolve off of the Hourly Data provided using the "Show Hourly Data" button.

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to US Units w/ kts" button until the relevant table displays °F.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Fahrenheit (eg, 21°F). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Traders see 31°C as the most likely peak for Panama City, Panama, today, with 32°C a close second, reflecting the city's typical September climatology of daily highs near 29–30°C during the rainy season. Persistent high humidity, frequent afternoon thunderstorms driven by the Intertropical Convergence Zone, and variable cloud cover from recent model runs have kept surface temperatures close to seasonal norms without strong warming or cooling signals. Official forecasts and recent observations show maxima clustering around 29–30°C, with any brief clearing potentially allowing brief spikes to 31–32°C before convection develops. Market-implied odds align with this narrow range, as historical September data and current steering patterns indicate low odds for extremes outside 30–32°C. Updated National Meteorological Service of Panama guidance or late-day observations remain the key near-term catalysts.

eventMetadata.context_description: Persistent rain and extensive cloud cover on September 7 are suppressing daytime heating in Tokyo, keeping forecast highs clustered around 26–28°C according to Japan Meteorological Agency and global model consensus. Southerly flow and high humidity further limit surface warming despite seasonal norms near 29°C, with hourly observations on September 6 already showing limited recovery under similar conditions. This scientific setup—reduced insolation from stratiform clouds and ongoing precipitation—explains trader emphasis on 27°C as the modal outcome, with lower probabilities assigned to clearer-sky scenarios that would allow brief spikes toward 29°C or above. Updated model runs and official briefings through the evening of September 6 will provide the next key data points before resolution.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent ensemble forecasts from ECMWF and supporting models indicate a southerly flow advecting warmer air into the Netherlands, positioning Amsterdam's September 7 maximum near 25–27°C under partly cloudy skies with light to moderate southwesterly winds. This consensus, with limited model spread and no significant frontal passages expected before peak heating, underpins the market's strong weighting toward 26°C at 47.5% and 25°C at 36.5% implied probability. Minor variations in cloud cover or boundary-layer mixing could shift the exact high by 1–2°C, consistent with the narrower probabilities assigned to 24°C and 27°C. Updated model runs tomorrow morning will provide the final refinement ahead of resolution.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

Updated JMA guidance and high-resolution model runs expected over the next 48 hours will likely refine the maximum before resolution.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Recent forecasts from multiple meteorological sources indicate a daytime high in Milan on September 8, 2026, most likely in the 32–33°C range under persistent high pressure, clear to partly cloudy skies, and light southerly winds that favor daytime heating.** 

Current model consensus (including runs referenced on sites like Worldmeteo, Yr.no, and Globalmeteo) shows peak temperatures reaching 32–34°C in the afternoon before any evening cooling or light shower activity, consistent with the market’s heaviest weighting on 32°C (42.5%) and 31°C (30.5%), followed by 33°C (15%). 

This aligns with an ongoing warm spell in early September, when observed highs have already hit 33–34°C on the 6th and 7th amid above-average conditions for the month (climatological September mean high near 25°C). A frontal system and cooler air are expected to arrive on the 9th, bringing showers and a sharp drop to the mid-20s°C, which limits upside risk for extremes above 34°C on the 8th. 

Traders are therefore pricing the narrow window around the forecast peak, with lower probabilities assigned to cooler outcomes (30°C or below at ~15% combined) or hotter outliers (35°C+ under 3%). Updated model runs and official Italian meteorological agency guidance over the next 24–48 hours remain the key near-term catalysts that could shift these implied probabilities.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Forecast models from sources like ECMWF and ICON-EU indicate Warsaw will experience southerly flow under building high pressure on September 8, supporting daytime maxima near 26–28°C with minimal cloud cover and negligible precipitation risk. This pattern follows cooler, more unsettled conditions earlier in the week, driving the recent upward shift in implied probabilities for 27°C as the most likely peak. Ensemble spreads remain modest but highlight sensitivity to exact timing of peak insolation and any afternoon convective development, keeping 26°C and 28°C as viable alternatives. Official verification will rely on the highest recorded value at the primary Warsaw meteorological station.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent National Weather Service guidance and ensemble model runs indicate a high near 86-87°F at Los Angeles International Airport on September 8, with partly cloudy skies and moderate onshore flow limiting stronger warming. Remnant moisture from distant Hurricane Marie is expected to keep marine-layer influence and cloud cover in check rather than suppress temperatures sharply, while light west-southwest winds and minimal precipitation support readings in the mid- to upper-80s range. Historical climatology places the September 8 average high near 76°F, so current conditions reflect a notable positive anomaly that narrows the distribution between the closely matched 84-85°F and 86-87°F market bins. Updated model guidance and morning observations on September 7 will refine whether any additional warming pushes the peak into the 88-89°F tier.

eventMetadata.context_description: Latest National Weather Service and ensemble forecasts show San Francisco highs on September 8 trending into the upper 70s to low 80s as high pressure builds and onshore marine flow weakens, allowing modest warming from the east. This follows early-September readings mostly in the upper 60s to low 70s under stronger westerlies and marine-layer influence. Differentiating the tightly bunched 78–85°F outcomes are small model differences in wind direction, afternoon cloud cover, and the precise strength of any downslope warming, all of which can shift peak readings by a few degrees in San Francisco’s variable microclimate. Traders are pricing the resulting forecast uncertainty, with resolution hinging on official observations at downtown or airport stations.
